task.title: Fix payment client timeouts

current_proposal.summary: Replace the pooling-only mitigation with the documented RetryPolicy fix: set max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=50, retain Timeout-only retry eligibility, verify the 50 ms jitter minimum separately from the existing cap test, and gate rollout on confirmed idempotency, verified rollout/monitoring/rollback tooling, and quantified downstream capacity thresholds.
plan_steps: Confirm the current RetryPolicy values from configuration or stored records before making the change.

Before production rollout, verify a preventive idempotency guarantee or safeguard for payment requests retried after SendError::Timeout. If no such guarantee can be confirmed from stored records or the downstream contract, do not roll out the retry increase and escalate the duplicate-payment risk for a documented decision; duplicate-payment monitoring alone is not treated as prevention.

Before production rollout, verify that gradual rollout, monitoring of attempts per request and retry bursts, and RetryPolicy rollback are actually available. If any of these cannot be confirmed, do not roll out and escalate for a documented decision rather than assuming the tooling exists.

Before production rollout, obtain documented downstream capacity figures and, from them, set and record quantified pass/fail thresholds for the load test and rollout, including downstream latency, error rate, and retry volume. Use the structural bound that max_attempts=3 permits at most 3 total attempts per original request (at most 3x volume for requests that time out). If quantified capacity or thresholds cannot be obtained and recorded, do not roll out and escalate rather than claiming the amplification is safe.
Set RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50, without increasing the attempt cap above 3.
Remove the previously proposed connection-pool, keep-alive, and separate connect/read timeout changes from scope because no provided record establishes that those settings are supported.
Run constraint_cap_is_three_attempts and tests confirming that only SendError::Timeout is retried up to max_attempts and that upstream errors are not retried.

Separately verify the configured values directly (by configuration inspection or an added assertion/test) that max_attempts equals 3 and jitter_ms is at least 50, so that a jitter_ms of 1-49 ms would fail verification even though it would pass constraint_cap_is_three_attempts.

Perform a bounded load or capacity test under transient SendError::Timeout conditions simulating up to the 3x worst-case attempt volume, verifying no request exceeds 3 attempts and jitter_ms is at least 50. Proceed only if the pre-recorded quantified downstream latency, error-rate, and retry-volume thresholds from the capacity step are met; if they are exceeded or were never established, halt and do not roll out.

Only after the idempotency, tooling, and capacity gates pass, roll out gradually while monitoring payment timeout rate, attempts per request, retry bursts, upstream latency and errors against the pre-recorded thresholds, and duplicate-payment indicators; roll back the RetryPolicy change if any pre-recorded threshold is crossed or duplicate-payment indicators worsen.

claims.statement: The revised configuration sets the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50, replacing the default max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0 and staying within the documented cap of 3 attempts with at least 50 ms jitter.
send_with_retries will retry only SendError::Timeout up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors will be returned at once without a retry.

constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails when max_attempts is above 3 or jitter_ms equals 0; it does not by itself enforce the documented minimum of 50 ms, so verification will separately assert that the configured jitter_ms is at least 50.

assumptions: The documented decision to set the payment-client RetryPolicy implies that max_attempts and jitter_ms are configurable in the deployed client.
A direct configuration check or additional test for jitter_ms >= 50 can be added or performed; no provided record describes an existing check that enforces that minimum.
uncertainties: No provided record documents an idempotency requirement, idempotency key, or downstream idempotency guarantee for payment requests retried after SendError::Timeout, so the duplicate-payment safeguard status is unknown until verified.
No provided record establishes support for separate connect/read timeouts or configurable connection-pool size and keep-alive, so those mechanisms are excluded rather than assumed.

The provided records do not quantify downstream capacity or safe latency, error-rate, or retry-volume thresholds beyond the documented 3-attempt cap and at-least-50 ms jitter requirement, so those thresholds must be obtained and recorded before rollout.
No provided record confirms that gradual rollout, retry-burst monitoring, or configuration rollback tooling exists, so availability is unknown until verified before rollout.
The provided records do not confirm whether transient SendError::Timeout is the sole cause of the observed user-facing payment timeouts.

items.description: Keeping the existing retry policy unchanged contradicts the documented decision to set max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and leaves the default max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0, which fails the cap test requiring non-zero jitter and conflicts with the constraint that outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter.

Limiting mitigation to pooling and timeout configuration and adding no retries conflicts with the documented fix because the default single attempt is recorded as the reason a transient upstream timeout surfaces to users and send_with_retries only retries SendError::Timeout.

No retrieved record supports the assumption that the payment client supports separate connect and read timeouts or configurable connection-pool size and keep-alive, so the proposed pooling and timeout mitigation may be unimplementable as described.

The claim that retries will follow a documented idempotency requirement is unsupported because the only documented retry-eligibility rule retries SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts and no retrieved record documents any idempotency requirement or idempotency key for payment requests.

Retrying a payment request after a SendError::Timeout without a documented idempotency guarantee creates a duplicate-payment risk because the downstream may have already processed the payment before the timeout, and monitoring duplicate-payment indicators after rollout does not prevent that outcome.

Increasing pool capacity and lengthening connect or read timeouts under load could amplify a downstream slowdown by sustaining more concurrent in-flight payments, a failure mode similar to the recorded 2026-08 outage where payment-client bursts amplified an upstream slowdown, and the proposal provides no load or capacity test to bound that risk.

The proposal includes no test step verifying constraint_cap_is_three_attempts or otherwise checking that max_attempts remains at or below 3 with non-zero jitter, so a non-compliant retry configuration could persist undetected.

assessments.note: No Valid record directly states the proposal's retry stance. Records show the documented decision requires max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms at least 50, the default is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0, the cap test fails at jitter_ms=0, and outbound retries must be capped at 3 with jitter; keeping the policy unchanged leaves that conflict.

No Valid record directly states the proposal adds no retries or supports separate connect/read timeouts and configurable pooling/keep-alive. The documented fix is setting RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3, the default single attempt is recorded as surfacing transient timeouts, and send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts.

No Valid record documents an idempotency requirement or key, or states post-change retries will follow one. The only documented eligibility record states retries only for SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts, with no idempotency condition.

proposal.summary: Mitigate payment-client load timeouts without changing the existing retry policy, by first identifying whether delays are in connection acquisition, connection establishment, or downstream reads, then tuning connection pooling/keep-alive and distinct connect/read timeouts accordingly.
plan_steps: Instrument connect time, read time, and connection-pool wait time to identify which timeout occurs under load.
Keep the existing retry policy unchanged while adjusting connection reuse, pool capacity, and connect/read timeout configuration based on the measurements.
Roll out gradually while monitoring timeout rate, payment errors, and duplicate-payment indicators, with rollback of the configuration change if those worsen.

claims.statement: This proposal does not increase retry attempts, expand retryable operations, or change retry backoff relative to the existing documented retry constraints.
This proposal adds no retries for payment requests; mitigation is limited to connection-pool/keep-alive configuration and explicit connect/read timeout configuration.
Any retry occurring after this change will follow the pre-existing documented retry-eligibility rules, including any documented idempotency requirement.

assumptions: Timeouts under load may involve transient downstream latency or connection-pool queueing that explicit timeout and pooling configuration can mitigate; this cause is not confirmed by any record provided here.
The payment client supports separate connect/read timeout settings and configurable connection-pool size and keep-alive.
Timeout, duplicate-payment, and error-rate monitoring is available for a gradual rollout and rollback.
uncertainties: No stored records were provided, so the current timeout values, connection-pool settings, maximum retry attempts, backoff policy, and retryable-error list are unknown.
The documented idempotency requirement for retrying payment requests, if any, was not provided.
The root cause of the load-related timeouts has not been confirmed; downstream latency limits, pool exhaustion, and service capacity remain unknown.
Safe replacement timeout and pool values cannot be determined without latency and load measurements from the stored incident or performance records.

chain.note: This run's events form a complete hash chain from genesis on their own: recomputing every record's hash and link from them alone verifies the run. head_hash is the hash of its last event. The chain is unsigned SHA-256. A successful check shows that the records received are internally consistent; it detects a change only against a hash obtained earlier, such as this receipt's head_hash or a published manifest. It cannot detect a run rewritten and re-hashed, a truncated tail or a deleted run, and it says nothing about whether the content is true.

receipt.proof_limitations: A proof marked valid means that Hyphae's verifier re-executed the request the proof sealed against its witness and accepted it at the anchor it was given (the pinned anchor wherever one is configured, always for the public snapshot). It covers the whole result of that request (for the sealed snapshot, the complete record list of the snapshot's project at that anchor), never a claim, even when the request's query is a claim's text, and a record's text is not byte-compared with the proof. A simulated proof checks nothing. Proofs do not establish that the content is true, relevant, or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.
